title: Daily Sky Summary — Sun + Moon source bank
readMeFirst: 72 records: 12 sunSummary, 60 moonSummary. No record is blank.
Only 192 of the 720 dropdown combinations are real skies. See assembly.geometry.
importAction 'replace' means the stored record is wrong and must be overwritten. There are 4.
importAction 'skip_if_present' means a live record exists that this file must not clobber. There is 1.
All 72 records are reviewStatus approved and serve in production. No row needs allowUnreviewed.
No text in this file derives from a third-party book. Verified at 6-gram against the whole Resources library.

assembly.note: Render exactly one Moon passage. Never stack the regular Moon and a special Moon.

templates.free: The Sun in {{sunSign}} {{sunSummary}}, while the Moon in {{moonSign}} {{moonSummary}}. {{currentRetrogradesSentence}}
templates.freeSameSign: The Sun in {{sunSign}} {{sunSummary}}, while the Moon there {{moonSummary}}. {{currentRetrogradesSentence}}
templates.conjunction: The Sun in {{sunSign}} {{sunSummary}}, while the {{eventLabel}} in the same sign {{moonSummary}}. {{currentRetrogradesSentence}}
templates.conjunctionMoonLed: The {{eventLabel}} in {{sign}} {{moonSummary}}, while the Sun there {{sunSummary}}. {{currentRetrogradesSentence}}
templates.opposition: The Sun in {{sunSign}} {{sunSummary}}, while the {{eventLabel}} in {{moonSign}} {{moonSummary}}. {{currentRetrogradesSentence}}

free.sameSignRule: When the regular Moon is in the Sun's own sign (12 of the 144), use templates.freeSameSign so the sign is not printed twice.

conjunction.why: A New Moon is the Sun and Moon at the same degree, so the Moon is always in the Sun's sign.

opposition.why: A Full Moon is the Sun and Moon exactly 180 degrees apart, so the Moon is always in the opposite sign.

adminEditor.moonSignField: When Moon Event is not 'regular', Moon Sign is derived, not free. Recommend bidirectional: changing either dropdown moves the other.

axisNaming.why: The template already supplies both signs. Several Full Moon clauses used to name the axis themselves; the Aries one has been corrected.

runtimeGuard.rule: For any event other than 'regular', derive sunSign and moonSign from the lunation's exact UTC timestamp, not from the local-noon transit stack.
runtimeGuard.why: On an ingress day the noon Sun sign and the lunation Moon sign can disagree and produce an impossible pair.
runtimeGuard.assertion: conjunction: moonSign == sunSign. opposition: moonSign == oppositions[sunSign]. Otherwise throw IMPOSSIBLE_SKY.
runtimeGuard.note: IMPOSSIBLE_SKY is an ephemeris bug, not a content gap. It must not fall through to the fallback ladder.

fallbackLadder.rule: authored moonSummary for this sign and event, reviewStatus approved
eclipse events only: base lunation record + eclipseLayer

fallbackLadder.action: render the Sun sentence alone and stop

assembly.neverRender: 'while the Lunar Eclipse is in Cancer' and any other subject-plus-linking-verb fragment. That is a content-role violation, and it is what the current build shows on every eclipse preview.
assembly.collisionRule: If the composed paragraph trips a lint, re-render using the Moon record's 'alt', else the Sun record's 'alt', else drop to tier 3. Alts are approved substitutes, not lesser copy.

eclipseLayer.why: Solar eclipse is a supercharged New Moon; lunar eclipse is a supercharged Full Moon. Two approvals cover all 24 eclipse combinations and keep the eclipse temperature identical across every sign.
eclipseLayer.usage: Tier 2 of the fallback ladder. With all 24 eclipse records now approved, tier 1 always resolves and this layer is a standing safety net rather than the working path. It matters again if an eclipse record is ever unpublished or a new event type is added.
eclipseLayer.solar: , and what begins here was not chosen
eclipseLayer.lunar: , and this ending arrives on its own schedule

temperatureRules.solar: A supercharged New Moon. It begins, interrupts, or reveals. No desire test, because the reader did not choose the event.
temperatureRules.lunar: A supercharged Full Moon, collapse-first. Endings arrive on their own schedule and are not softened into choices.

phaseBank.note: Tier 3 of the ladder. General phase phrases from private-author-source.invalid. Reference language: they do not authorize filling a sign-specific record.

sourceStatusTiers.meaning: private-author-source.invalid sentence, grammar, pronoun or trim only
row already approved in the TLDR corpus

validation.grammarFrame: verb_first_3sg: every sunSummary and moonSummary is verb-first, third person singular present, no leading subject, no terminal punctuation.
blockingLints: sign repetition: the same sign name printed twice in one paragraph
sun sign named inside the moon clause
axis double-naming: axisNaming on while the clause already names the axis
em dash, en dash or exclamation mark present
warningLints: verb collision: both clauses open on the same verb
repeated content word across the two clauses

warning: repeated word ['between', 'space']: Sun Aquarius / Moon Pisces [resolve with moon alt or sun alt]
repeated word ['between']: Sun Aquarius / Moon Aries [resolve with sun alt]
repeated word ['fire']: Sun Aries / Moon Leo [resolve with moon alt or sun alt]
repeated word ['self']: Sun Leo / Moon Libra [resolve with sun alt]
repeated word ['self']: Sun Leo / New Moon Leo [resolve with sun alt]
repeated word ['space']: Sun Aquarius / Moon Scorpio [resolve with moon alt or sun alt]
lastRun.note: Warnings are resolvable at render time by the collisionRule: re-render with the Moon record's alt where one exists.

provenance.rule: No text in this file derives from a third-party book. Books in the Resources library are reference lane, never served verbatim, per tldr-astro-cc-books-reference-pack.md.
provenance.verified: 6-gram overlap check, stricter than the project's 8-gram rule, run against every extractable book in the Resources library: Moonology (Boland), Where Dragons Dance, Your Secret Moon, The Book of the Moon (Forrest), The Career Astrology, Karmic Astrology, The Astrology of Awakening, Astrology Karma & Transformation, Hellenistic Astrology for Beginners, The Soul System of Tarot, Skymates 2, The Astrology of You and Me, Do You Love Me, Astrology and Relationships, plus Celestial Alchemy and all 52 pre-extracted .txt files.
provenance.result: Zero matches against any third-party book. One 6-gram coincidence in the wider library ('between what we know and what', Elizabeth Spring's North Node Astrology) inside a clause that is a verbatim private-author-source.invalid sentence. Matches against the TLDR corpus are expected and confirm derivation from owner material.
provenance.moonologyNote: Moonology was read for one structural fact only: it heads its sections 'New Moon (or solar eclipse) in {sign}' and 'Full Moon (or lunar eclipse) in {sign}', which independently confirms the eclipse-as-intensifier model behind eclipseLayer. No sentence from it entered any record.
provenance.celestialAlchemyNote: Project Author's own Celestial Alchemy (2023) carries a complete Sun-through-the-signs set plus Sun in houses 1-12 and Sun house transits 1-12. It is written in the natal register ('With your Sun in Aries, you radiate energy and courage') and is therefore the right source for a natal Sun surface and the house layer, not for this sky summary. Log it there separately. Its PDF extraction drops ligatures; repair before storing.

openRulings: Virgo sunSummary: the live line is kept and the import skips it. Switch importAction to upsert if you want the site-sourced alt instead.
Export any other live sunSummary records from the app store, so this import is a diff rather than a build.

approvalLog.scope: All 26 rows previously marked needs_review: 20 eclipse records written to the locked eclipse rules, 3 Moon records and 3 Sun records condensed from the TLDR corpus. Plus both eclipseLayer clauses.
approvalLog.traceability: Each promoted record keeps its origin in priorStatus. Nothing about how a line was written has been erased; only its serving state changed.
approvalLog.revisit: To pull any single row back, set its reviewStatus to needs_review and restore sourceStatus from priorStatus.
